tools.name: list_catalog
tools.description: List live BotSupply SKUs, credit prices, short descriptions, and what a purchase does not include. Payloads stay behind purchase. recipe.book-table, when listed, is recipe documentation only and does not place a reservation.

tools.name: open_wallet
tools.description: Create a wallet and return wallet_id plus api_key once, with balance_credits 0. Same as POST /v1/wallets. This does not look up an existing wallet. Keep the api_key; later tools need it as Authorization: Bearer or as api_key.

tools.name: get_balance
tools.description: Return the authenticated wallet id and prepaid credit balance. Same as GET /v1/balance. Does not return the API key.

tools.name: purchase
tools.description: Buy one live catalog SKU with prepaid credits. Sends { sku } to POST /v1/purchase and returns that JSON, including the pack or recipe payload. Does not place a reservation. recipe.book-table is documentation the buying agent runs itself. An unknown SKU is rejected. Insufficient balance returns an er

tools.name: create_checkout
tools.description: Start a Stripe Checkout credit top-up. Same as POST /v1/wallets/:id/checkout. Returns the checkout url (open that URL; it keeps Stripe's hosted-page fragment). credits is an integer from 500 to 100000 ($5 minimum). Credits are applied only after Stripe reports the session paid. Returns the API error

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "open_wallet" references sensitive artifacts (api_key, authorization, bearer). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: open_wallet, create_checkout, record_approval · Private data: open_wallet, get_balance, create_job, record_approval, set_receipt_visibility, record_payment, get_receipt, verify_receipt · Public sink: open_wallet, purchase, create_checkout, create_job, release_job, refund_job, record_approval, set_receipt_visibility, attach_proof, record_payment.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: open_wallet, create_checkout, record_approval · Private data: open_wallet, get_balance, create_job, record_approval, set_receipt_visibility, record_payment, get_receipt, verify_receipt · Public sink: open_wallet, purchase, create_checkout, create_job, release_job, refund_job, record_approval, set_receipt_visibility, attach_proof, record_payment

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "create_checkout" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
